messages:
maria chen: quick sync on the prompt-cache contract — hit a couple odd edgecases while testing a canary build

samir patel: send examples pls, i can try reproduce locally

maria chen: minimal repro + questions below. observed behavior: identical user prompt + model but different system prompt casing produced cache MISS. also saw users trying to rely on x-cache boolean which we changed earlier — need compat story

kai li: casing diff makes sense if we use raw prompt string in key. we should canonicalize (trim, normalize whitespace, lowercase system prompt?) but lowercase might be risky for user content

jia wong: what about structured prompts (tool calls / function schema)? those should be part of the key too, otherwise different call args could collide

maria chen: agree on structured. proposal: cache key is sha256 of canonicalized object with fields: model_id, model_version_hash, normalized_system_prompt, normalized_user_prompt, serialized_tools_spec, temperature_bucket, response_format_hint, streaming=false/true

samir patel: temp_bucket? explain

maria chen: bucket temperature into [0, 0.2), [0.2,0.7), [0.7,1] — reduces cache fragmentation but preserves semantics for deterministic vs exploratory queries

kai li: we should also include max_tokens (or max_output_len_bucket). otherwise truncation differences will change output

jia wong: how do we signal cache hits to clients? some teams prefer header-based, others prefer body-level metadata for analytics

maria chen: plan: add both a response header and body metadata. header for lightweight infra routing, body for downstream apps. header: `x-redwood-cache: HIT; key=sha256:abcd1234; ttl=45` body snippet: ```json
{"cache": {"hit": true, "key_hint": "sha256:abcd1234", "ttl_secs": 45}}
```

samir patel: keep old header name (x-cache-hit) for backward compat? some customers already parse it

maria chen: yes — we'll populate `x-cache-hit: 1|0` for compatibility and mark it deprecated in 2 quarters. add deprecation note in docs and console alerts for customers using it

kai li: invalidation story? how to evict when model version / quantization changes, or when prompt templates are updated

maria chen: two-layer invalidation: 1) versioned cache namespace driven by model_version_hash; when model is updated we bump namespace so old keys are ignored 2) soft tag invalidation for prompt templates: clients can send `cache_tags: ["promo_v2_template"]` on requests and owners can bulk-invalidate tag sets from control plane

jia wong: caching user-specific content — we must be careful with PII. proposal: by default keys do NOT include user_id. add explicit `cache_scope: "user"` opt-in flag for orgs that need per-user caches and have consent/compliance

samir patel: tests we need: canonicalization unit tests, header/body parity, tag invalidation e2e, model bump fuzz test

maria chen: i'll open a PR with the canonicalizer + unit tests and a small endpoint that returns the key_hint in dev env. can you add infra tests and a control-plane invalidate endpoint, @samir @kai?

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: canary/eng-platform/prompt-cache-fix -> prod on 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC

maria chen: action items:
- maria: PR with canonicalizer + unit tests (in progress)
- samir: infra/e2e tests + invalidate endpoint
- kai: add header compatibility and docs update for deprecation timeline
- jia: review privacy scoped caching wording and ask legal if needed

samir patel: sounds good, will pick up infra tomorrow morning

kai li: lgtm — thanks for the clear proposal

jia wong: one more thought — include `cache_control` hint param clients can set (none|public|private) which maps to behavior and TTL defaults

maria chen: good call. i'll add that to the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
